question: Resolve a list of gene symbols to verified ENSDARG IDs and flag any that do not resolve (positive NOT_FOUND). Why must IDs never come from memory?
direct_answer:
ORTHOLOG MAPPING (symbol -> ENSDARG, Danio rerio / GRCz11), each ID taken ONLY from a live tool response, never from memory. No explicit input list was supplied, so I ran a small representative project-domain set (pronephros markers) plus a deliberate not-found probe.

RESOLVED (3): pax2a -> ENSDARG00000028148; wt1a -> ENSDARG00000031420; osr1 -> ENSDARG00000014091. All three returned status=success from ensembl_lookup_gene (species=danio_rerio, assembly GRCz11) with matching ZFIN-sourced descriptions, and all three cross-check EXACTLY against the DATA INAMOVIBLE store (verified_identifiers.json, store_version 2026-06-23.1).

FLAGGED NOT_FOUND (1, positive): clcnkb -> NOT_FOUND. Ensembl returned HTTP 400 "No valid lookup found for symbol clcnkb" for danio_rerio. This is a *positive* absence (looked, does not resolve) per resolve_id.py NOT_FOUND semantics, corroborated by the store record (ensdarg=null, confidence=0.0). Positive NOT_FOUND is a result, not a failure: it converts a would-be silent wrong-ID into a loud, explicit miss. Caveat: it means "no danio_rerio gene carries the symbol clcnkb," not "no zebrafish ortholog exists" — a homolog may exist under a different official symbol.

WHY IDs MUST NEVER COME FROM MEMORY: ENSDARG accessions are opaque, checksum-free 11-digit strings; a hallucinated one is syntactically valid and silently wrong, so the error is undetectable at the point of use and propagates into expression lookups, evidence_cited, and downstream analysis as retractable claims. This is not hypothetical in this project: the May 8-9 2026 session had 5/11 ENSDARG IDs (~45%) and 1 PMID wrong from memory; the 2026-06 corruption had 15/16 marker IDs in 01_schoels_analysis.py wrong plus a wt1a false-positive (docs/findings/2026-06-10-schoels-phase1-id-corruption.md). The structural fix (CLAUDE.md §7 anti-fabrication gate, §10 step 7): resolve() against the verified store first; on NOT_FOUND, verify against the authoritative source (Ensembl REST) and CACHE THE RAW RESPONSE (§7.9) before use — an AI-processed summary is not verification because the AI layer can hallucinate the very field being verified. IDs in scripts come from resolve_id.require() (raises on NOT_FOUND), never hardcoded from recall.

Use Ensembl_lookup_gene_by_symbol / ensembl_get_xrefs_by_name instead (VIABLE equivalents; ensembl_lookup_gene direct symbol lookup was sufficient and returns the canonical ENSDARG + assembly, so no extra call needed — 'prueba pequeno')

Report a single aggregated confidence hiding sub-claim asymmetry (considered confidence_by_subclaim; sub-claims are all high-evidence [live+store double-confirmed], so a single 0.96 is defensible; residual uncertainty is the NOT_FOUND-vs-no-ortholog nuance, flagged in gaps)

framework_applied: Logic-LM (Symbolic Verification) — per reasoning-frameworks-catalog.md §5 Logic-LM: "for any task whose criteria are formalizable; produces results perfectly calibrated by construction." Symbol->ENSDARG resolution is a formalizable binary predicate (does symbol X resolve to a valid ENSDARG in the authoritative Ensembl danio_rerio namespace, yes/no); the deterministic resolve_id/verify_output gate is explicitly Logic-LM-class (not an LLM), so the verification step is symbolic, not neural.
